Statement from Reliance Industries 

In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record.

Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation,  homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people.

That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances.

At Reliance,  we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world.

We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.

candidates.text:
Last year I thought Threads was an existential risk to X. 

When Meta puts its full weight behind something -- by injecting the app into Instagram, it’s DEFCON 5:

You have to squeeze out every last drop of growth from all available surfaces to save the app.

However, I started to realize that the opposite was happening:

It was strengthening X.

If you look at any announcement by Zuck, you will see the most rude & toxic comments on the internet. 

But when he makes those same announcements on X, people are thrilled about how he’s pushing humanity forward. X is a place where people are excited about the future, so it’s no surprise he and his top lieutenants are using it more than their own app.

Threads — and Bluesky — have effectively quarantined some of the worst people on the internet. 

And so I had an epiphany: those apps are X’s anti-abuse systems.

candidates.text:
We launched a news site this week, so here's why we built it, in 3 parts

1. We were already reading all of it

Every day our pipeline pulls crypto and AI news from X and the trade press so we can decide what to post. Last week that was over a thousand stories, and once we'd read and sourced them, most of it just sat in a database

If your team already does this kind of research for content, it's an asset. It only looks like overhead because nobody outside the team ever sees it

2. So we put it on a page

https://t.co/KeIWIAX4sF is every day's news in one place, sorted by date, with each story linked to where it came from

I think a daily reading habit is worth more than any single post going viral. People come back to things that are useful every morning, and that's an audience you own instead of renting from a feed

3. Sponsors come once the traffic is real

For now it's free. Once enough people read it every day, we'll open a few sponsor slots for teams that want to be in front of them

It's the same playbook we run for clients, so it felt a bit silly not to run it for ourselves first
